# Ask Conversation Scope

## How To Build

A AskConversationScope should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A AskConversationScope should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, intergration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../../ui/theme/index.md#theme-scope): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Concept

### Pitch

The questions asked from the Ask tab, read as a chat: every question and its answer, one after another, in a pane of its own beside the tasks, with each new conversation clearly marked where it begins.

### Shape

#### Description

While the [ChatInputScope](../chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope)'s Ask tab is selected, the [BodyScope](../../application/Body.md#body-scope) splits in two, side by side, above the chat input: the body's tab bar and the selected tab's contents on the left, and this pane on the right. It goes when another tab is selected, the left side taking the body's full width again, and comes back as it was, scrolled where it was, when Ask is selected again. Nothing slides as it comes and goes.
It is drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../../ui/theme/index.md#theme-scope)'s roles, on the same base surface as the selected tab's contents beside it, with the theme's line between the two halves. Along its top runs a header as tall as the body's tab bar, 32 pixels, on the tab bar's background with the theme's line beneath it, reading "Questions" at its left, with 12 pixels of padding, and at its right how many questions it holds, muted.

#### Split

The pane starts at half the width of the space it shares with the left side. The line between them is a resize edge: hovering it shows the resize cursor for left and right and a thin line in the theme's accent, and dragging it moves it, following the pointer exactly, from 25% to 75% of that space, both sides laid out anew at each width. The width it is dragged to is kept for as long as the application runs, for every project, and none of it is saved.

#### Conversation

The pane lists every question of the project, those saved with it and those asked since, running or finished, oldest at the top and the newest at the bottom, the way a chat reads. Each is a message and its reply. The question is shown as it was typed, not as it was compiled, in a box on the theme's raised surface, faintly tinted Ask's colour, as the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope) colours it, with corners rounded 6 pixels, set against the pane's right edge and at most 80% of its width, wrapping within that, with anything it was sent with, attached text and images, listed beneath its text as the chat input lists them. Beneath the box, at its right, sits a small muted line with the time it was asked and, once it is finished, a Resend button, which asks the question again as the [PromptSendingScope](../sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) says, the new question coming in at the bottom.
Its answer follows beneath it, as a chat reply rather than a task: against the pane's left edge, across the pane's full width, with no box. The answer is read as prose, not as a list of what the harness did.

#### Answers

An answer is not drawn as a [TaskTableScope](../../../ui/components/task-table/index.md#task-table-scope): it has no columns, no Type badges or Status labels, and no lines between rows. What is shown is the answer's reply text, the reply rows after the harness's last tool call, as the table's collapsed steps count them, rendered as markdown in the body's text colour, one paragraph after another, as a message in a chat is. Code blocks, lists, tables, and links in it are rendered as markdown renders them anywhere. An answer with no tool calls is all reply text; a finished answer with nothing to show reads "No answer.", muted.
Everything the harness did before the answer, its tool calls and any reply text between them, is gathered into one line above the answer, small and muted, beside a right chevron, summing it up, as "Read 3 files, searched twice, ran 1 command" or "Worked through 6 steps" where it can't be summed up by kind. Clicking it expands the steps in place, beneath it and above the answer, as compact muted lines, one per step: a tool call as its tool's name, muted, then its most telling argument, shortened as the [TaskTableScope](../../../ui/components/task-table/index.md#task-table-scope)'s tool calls are, and reply text between them as muted markdown; clicking it again collapses them. It starts collapsed, and stays as it was left for as long as the application runs. An answer whose harness did nothing before replying has no such line.
While the harness works on a question, a status line takes that line's place: a spinner and the latest thing the harness did, muted, with a Stop button at its right that stops just that question, leaving the others running. Reply text streams in beneath it as prose as the harness writes it; text it goes on to follow with a tool call joins the steps once the call comes, so only the answer is left as prose. Once the question finishes, the status line becomes the summary line.
A question that failed ends its answer with the error, in the theme's error colour, beneath whatever reply came before it. One that was stopped ends with "Stopped", muted. Neither is shown as a status in a table.
Questions are 16 pixels apart, and a question's answer 8 pixels beneath it.
Questions asked while another is still running come in at the bottom in the order they were asked, each answered in its own place as its harness goes, so answers can be filling in at once.

#### New Conversation

Where a new conversation begins, it is clearly marked: above the first question of each conversation, the first question in the pane included, runs a divider across the pane's full width, a line in Ask's colour at either side of a label reading "New conversation", then, muted, the date and time its first question was asked. A question starts a new conversation as its saved record says, in its hidden anchor's newConversation, as the [ChatInputScope](../chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) says; a question saved before that was recorded carries on the one above it, unless it is the first. A question asked while another was running carries on a copy of that conversation, as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) says, and is not marked.
Pressing New conversation for questions puts the divider in at the bottom of the pane straight away, beneath the last question, reading "New conversation" with no time, so it is plain that the next question starts with no context; the time is filled in once that question is asked. Pressed again with nothing asked since, it adds no second divider.

#### Scrolling

The pane scrolls, with a [ScrollbarScope](../../../ui/components/scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar-scope), and opens scrolled to the bottom, on the newest question, the first time it is shown. While it is at the bottom it stays locked there, following each question asked and each answer as it grows; scrolling up unlocks it, and scrolling back to the bottom locks it again. Asking a question always scrolls it to the bottom and locks it. However many questions it holds, and however long their answers, it lays out only what is in view: each question, divider, summary line, and block of an answer's markdown is drawn as it scrolls into view, so a long conversation costs no more to show, scroll, or resize than a short one.

#### Empty

With no question asked yet, the pane reads "No questions yet. Ask one below.", muted, centred in it.

#### Selecting Text

The text of any question, answer, or expanded step in the pane can be selected by dragging across it, as any text can. A drag that selects text ending within the pane shows a [SelectionPopoverScope](../../../ui/components/selection-popover/index.md#selection-popover-scope) with two buttons, "Copy", with a copy icon, and "Attach to prompt", with a paperclip icon. Copy puts the selected text on the clipboard; Attach to prompt adds it to the prompt as an attachment. Either one clears the selection, and the popover closes when the pane goes.

#### Elsewhere

While another tab is selected, the questions still running stay in view as small rows stacked directly above the chat input's tabs, the newest nearest them, each showing its first line and the latest thing the harness did, in a column that pushes what is above it up rather than covering it, up to 240 pixels tall and scrolling beyond that. A question leaves the stack once it finishes. Clicking one selects the Ask tab, the pane scrolled to that question. There is no stack while Ask is selected: its questions are in the pane.

#### Projects

The pane shows the questions of the project on screen, as the [OpenProjectsScope](../../open-projects/index.md#open-projects-scope) says, and each project keeps how far its pane was scrolled and whether it was locked to the bottom while the application runs; questions of other projects carry on running in the background.
# Harness Integration Scope

## Concept

### Pitch

Uses the one-off version of a coding harness for the selected ProjectDirectoryScope: `claude -p`, `codex exec`, or `opencode run`, whichever the user chose. Each run carries on a conversation, so the harness keeps its context between requests.

### Shape

#### Description

Should always run in auto mode.
The project's system prompt, its system template filled in, as the [ModeSystemPromptsScope](../prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts-scope) says, is appended to the harness's own system prompt, for example with `--append-system-prompt`, the same for every prompt of a conversation whatever its mode. The compiled systemPrompt of a prompt's hidden anchor, its mode's instructions, heads the prompt's own message instead.
The prompt is given to the harness on its standard input, and what the harness does is streamed back as it happens. A task's run takes its prompt as a stream of messages rather than a single one, so it can be fed more while it works, as its feeding says.
Its directory, which a system prompt's HARNESS_DIRECTORY stands for, is that of the harness in use: .claude, .codex, or .opencode.
Spec tasks, a Chain prompt's spec steps, and questions run the harness in a container the application owns, as the [ContainerEnvironmentScope](../container-environment/index.md#container-environment-scope) says, which holds only what their mode may use; Code tasks and a Chain prompt's code step do too while the project's "Run code tasks in a container" option is on. Every other run, Code while the option is off, Freeform, and the application's own, runs the harness on the host, in the project directory. Either way the harness is run, prompted, and read just as this says.

#### Harnesses

The harness in use is the one picked in the [SettingsWindowScope](../settings-window/index.md#settings-window-scope): Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode, Claude Code until another is picked. It is remembered for the user, as the [UserPreferencesScope](../user-preferences/index.md#user-preferences-scope) says, not for a project. Every run the application starts goes to it, the tasks, the questions, the palette's file search, the one-off runs, and the notes, commit messages, and prompt titles it writes, and everything else works the same whichever it is. A run already going when another is picked finishes with the harness it started with, and a conversation is only carried on by the harness it began with; the next request with another harness starts a new one.
Each harness is run its own way, streaming what it does as a line of JSON per event, which is read into the same reply, tool calls, usage, and result, whichever harness wrote it:

- Claude Code is `claude -p`, in auto mode, the system prompt given with `--append-system-prompt`, a conversation carried on with `--resume`, and a copy of one with `--fork-session`.
- Codex is `codex exec`, with `--full-auto` and `--json`, the prompt read from its standard input, a conversation carried on with `resume`.
- OpenCode is `opencode run`, with `--format json`, a conversation carried on with `--session`.

Codex and OpenCode take no system prompt of their own, so it is given ahead of the prompt, marked off from it. Neither can carry on a copy of a conversation, so a question asked while another is running starts a new conversation with them instead. The notes, commit messages, and prompt titles are written with a small model where the harness can be told one, Claude Code's haiku, and with the harness's default model otherwise.
When the harness picked isn't installed, a run on the host fails saying that it can't be run, as any run that can't be started does. A run in a container uses the harness in its image instead, and fails, where Podman isn't installed or can't run, as the [ContainerEnvironmentScope](../container-environment/index.md#container-environment-scope) says.

#### Protected Locations

Only a run on the host has protected locations. A run in a container has none, since nothing it mustn't touch is mounted there, as the [ContainerEnvironmentScope](../container-environment/index.md#container-environment-scope) says: it isn't guarded, and its harness is given no rule against reading or editing anything.
Where the harness takes rules for what its tools may do, as Claude Code does with `--disallowedTools`, a run on the host is told what its mode keeps it off. A Code task is told it may not edit the spec location, and a Spec task the code location; the application puts back whatever changes there all the same, and says so in the task's output as a passive notice, never an error, as the [TaskTableScope](../../ui/components/task-table/index.md#task-table-scope) says. A Code task and a question from the Ask tab are also told they may not read the spec location, alongside that, so they read the compiled reference instead, as the [ModeSystemPromptsScope](../prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts-scope) says. This rule is only a nudge, and doesn't enforce anything, since a shell command can still read the files, and nothing puts anything back or stops the run when one does. A harness that takes no such rules is told nothing of either.

#### Feeding

A task's run is given its prompt as a stream of messages: Claude Code with `--input-format stream-json`, each message written as a line of JSON on the harness's standard input, which stays open for as long as the run lasts. The run's first message is the task's compiled prompt, as ever, and each message sent to the task after it, from the [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope), is written as another.
A message reaches the harness when it finishes what it is doing rather than interrupting it, so a run that is mid-tool-call takes it once that call is over. The harness echoes each message back as it takes it in, with `--replay-user-messages`. A message taken in between turns is answered with a result of its own, and one taken while a turn is under way is answered within that turn, sharing its result.
A run can also start work in the background that goes on after its turn ends: Claude Code's subagents, shell commands run in the background, such as a long build, and any other kind of background task it adds later. Every such task holds the run open, whatever its kind. The run keeps each background task that has started and not yet ended, by its id: one starts when the harness says a task has started, and ends when the harness notifies that task's end, whatever it ended as. A notification doesn't say what kind of task it is, so it is matched by id against those seen starting. The harness wakes the run when a background task ends, so it can act on what came of it.
A result no longer ends the task on its own. The run's last result is the first to come once every message sent has been taken in and no background task is still going. A result that comes before then, while a message sent hasn't been taken in or a background task is still going, is only an answer: the task keeps running, its input stays open, and more can still be sent to it. At the last result the run's input is closed, but the task is only shown as finished once the harness's process has exited as well, and it then finishes in the state of that last result; until the process exits, the task keeps running. A process that exits without a last result finishes the task as a run with no result does, failed. A run that is stopped closes its input and ends straight away, whatever is still going in the background, since its whole process group is ended with it.
Codex's `codex exec` and OpenCode's `opencode run` read a single prompt and can't be fed more while they work, so a task running with either takes its prompt as ever and can't be sent more.
Questions, the palette's file search, the one-off runs, and the notes, commit messages, and prompt titles each take a single prompt, as ever.

#### Images

Images attached to a prompt, as the [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) says, are given to the harness as it takes them: to Claude Code as image content blocks, base64-encoded with their media type, in the same stream-json user message as the prompt's text, after it; to Codex with an `--image` argument per image; and to OpenCode with a `--file` argument per image. A message fed to a running Claude Code task carries its images the same way, and a Claude Code run that isn't fed more but has images is given its prompt as a stream-json message too, so the images can go with it. Codex's options end with `--` before the prompt when it is given images. Questions take images as tasks do.

#### Context

The harness keeps its context between requests instead of starting fresh each time. Each lane of the [PromptSendingScope](../prompt-mode/sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) carries on a conversation of its own, so nothing a task of one lane read reaches a task of the other: the spec lane's, carried on by Spec tasks and a Chain prompt's spec steps, and the code lane's, carried on by Code tasks, a Chain prompt's code step, and Freeform tasks. Each task sent carries on its own lane's, and since a lane runs one task at a time, two tasks never carry on the same conversation at once. A Chain prompt's steps hand on to each other as text, the prompt and what the step before replied, as the [ModeSystemPromptsScope](../prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts-scope) says, so the handoff crosses lanes whatever each lane's conversation holds. When the project is opened, each lane carries on the latest conversation among its own tasks in the history, a Chain task by the lane of the step it was.
A run in a container keeps its lane's sessions in that lane's volume, and a run on the host where the harness keeps them on the host, as the [ContainerEnvironmentScope](../container-environment/index.md#container-environment-scope) says, so a conversation is only carried on where it began: turning the project's "Run code tasks in a container" option on or off starts the code lane on a new conversation at its next task.
Questions from the Ask tab share a separate conversation of their own, and when the project is opened they carry on the latest conversation among the questions saved with it. A question asked while another is running carries on a copy of that conversation, so questions running at the same time never write over each other. A conversation is only carried on in the project it began in, each open project keeping its own tasks' and questions' conversations while it is in the background, and if one can't be carried on, the next request starts a new one. Each run applies its own prompt's systemPrompt, even when it carries on a conversation begun in a different mode. The palette's file search always starts fresh.
A conversation can be left for a new one, from the chat input's New conversation button, as the [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) says, which leaves the conversation of the lane it is used for: the next request in it starts a new conversation with no context, and the one left is not carried on again, not by a run of it still going, nor by the project's history. Leaving it is kept with the project, as the [ProjectDataScope](../project-data/index.md#project-data-scope) says, so a project opened after a lane's or the questions' conversation was left starts a new one there too, rather than carrying on the latest conversation in its history, until a run after the reset begins one of its own. How much context a conversation holds is known from what the harness reports with each reply: everything the model was given, cached or not, and what it wrote, as of its latest reply; replies of subagents don't count.

#### Baked Prompts

[BakedSystemPromptsScope](./baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts-scope)

#### One Off Runs

What is shown is the answer's reply text, the reply rows after the harness's last tool call, as the table's collapsed steps count them, rendered as markdown in the body's text colour, one paragraph after another, as a message in a chat is. Code blocks, lists, tables, and links in it are rendered as markdown renders them anywhere. An answer with no tool calls is all reply text; a finished answer with nothing to show reads "No answer.", muted.
Everything the harness did before the answer, its tool calls and any reply text between them, is gathered into one line above the answer, small and muted, beside a right chevron, summing it up, as "Read 3 files, searched twice, ran 1 command" or "Worked through 6 steps" where it can't be summed up by kind. Clicking it expands the steps in place, beneath it and above the answer, as compact muted lines, one per step: a tool call as its tool's name, muted, then its most telling argument, shortened as the [TaskTableScope](../../../ui/components/task-table/index.md#task-table-scope)'s tool calls are, and reply text between them as muted markdown; clicking it again collapses them. It starts collapsed, and stays as it was left for as long as the application runs. An answer whose harness did nothing before replying has no such line.
While the harness works on a question, a status line takes that line's place: a spinner and the latest thing the harness did, muted, with a Stop button at its right that stops just that question, leaving the others running. Reply text streams in beneath it as prose as the harness writes it; text it goes on to follow with a tool call joins the steps once the call comes, so only the answer is left as prose. Once the question finishes, the status line becomes the summary line.
A question that failed ends its answer with the error, in the theme's error colour, beneath whatever reply came before it. One that was stopped ends with "Stopped", muted. Neither is shown as a status in a table.
Questions are 16 pixels apart, and a question's answer 8 pixels beneath it.
Questions asked while another is still running come in at the bottom in the order they were asked, each answered in its own place as its harness goes, so answers can be filling in at once.

#### New Conversation

Where a new conversation begins, it is clearly marked: above the first question of each conversation, the first question in the pane included, runs a divider across the pane's full width, a line in Ask's colour at either side of a label reading "New conversation", then, muted, the date and time its first question was asked. A question starts a new conversation as its saved record says, in its hidden anchor's newConversation, as the [ChatInputScope](../chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) says; a question saved before that was recorded carries on the one above it, unless it is the first. A question asked while another was running carries on a copy of that conversation, as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) says, and is not marked.
Pressing New conversation for questions puts the divider in at the bottom of the pane straight away, beneath the last question, reading "New conversation" with no time, so it is plain that the next question starts with no context; the time is filled in once that question is asked. Pressed again with nothing asked since, it adds no second divider.

#### Scrolling

The pane scrolls, with a [ScrollbarScope](../../../ui/components/scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar-scope), and opens scrolled to the bottom, on the newest question, the first time it is shown. While it is at the bottom it stays locked there, following each question asked and each answer as it grows; scrolling up unlocks it, and scrolling back to the bottom locks it again. Asking a question always scrolls it to the bottom and locks it. However many questions it holds, and however long their answers, it lays out only what is in view: each question, divider, summary line, and block of an answer's markdown is drawn as it scrolls into view, so a long conversation costs no more to show, scroll, or resize than a short one.

#### Empty

With no question asked yet, the pane reads "No questions yet. Ask one below.", muted, centred in it.

#### Selecting Text

The text of any question, answer, or expanded step in the pane can be selected by dragging across it, as any text can. A drag that selects text ending within the pane shows a [SelectionPopoverScope](../../../ui/components/selection-popover/index.md#selection-popover-scope) with two buttons, "Copy", with a copy icon, and "Attach to prompt", with a paperclip icon. Copy puts the selected text on the clipboard; Attach to prompt adds it to the prompt as an attachment. Either one clears the selection, and the popover closes when the pane goes.

#### Elsewhere

While another tab is selected, the questions still running stay in view as small rows stacked directly above the chat input's tabs, the newest nearest them, each showing its first line and the latest thing the harness did, in a column that pushes what is above it up rather than covering it, up to 240 pixels tall and scrolling beyond that. A question leaves the stack once it finishes. Clicking one selects the Ask tab, the pane scrolled to that question. There is no stack while Ask is selected: its questions are in the pane.

#### Projects

The pane shows the questions of the project on screen, as the [OpenProjectsScope](../../open-projects/index.md#open-projects-scope) says, and each project keeps how far its pane was scrolled and whether it was locked to the bottom while the application runs; questions of other projects carry on running in the background.
# Harness Integration Scope

## Concept

### Pitch

Uses the one-off version of a coding harness for the selected ProjectDirectoryScope: `claude -p`, `codex exec`, or `opencode run`, whichever the user chose. Each run carries on a conversation, so the harness keeps its context between requests.

### Shape

#### Description

Should always run in auto mode.
The project's system prompt, its system template filled in, as the [ModeSystemPromptsScope](../prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts-scope) says, is appended to the harness's own system prompt, for example with `--append-system-prompt`, the same for every prompt of a conversation whatever its mode. The compiled systemPrompt of a prompt's hidden anchor, its mode's instructions, heads the prompt's own message instead.
The prompt is given to the harness on its standard input, and what the harness does is streamed back as it happens. A task's run takes its prompt as a stream of messages rather than a single one, so it can be fed more while it works, as its feeding says.
Its directory, which a system prompt's HARNESS_DIRECTORY stands for, is that of the harness in use: .claude, .codex, or .opencode.
Spec tasks, a Chain prompt's spec steps, and questions run the harness in a container the application owns, as the [ContainerEnvironmentScope](../container-environment/index.md#container-environment-scope) says, which holds only what their mode may use; Code tasks and a Chain prompt's code step do too while the project's "Run code tasks in a container" option is on. Every other run, Code while the option is off, Freeform, and the application's own, runs the harness on the host, in the project directory. Either way the harness is run, prompted, and read just as this says.

#### Harnesses

The harness in use is the one picked in the [SettingsWindowScope](../settings-window/index.md#settings-window-scope): Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode, Claude Code until another is picked. It is remembered for the user, as the [UserPreferencesScope](../user-preferences/index.md#user-preferences-scope) says, not for a project. Every run the application starts goes to it, the tasks, the questions, the palette's file search, the one-off runs, and the notes, commit messages, and prompt titles it writes, and everything else works the same whichever it is. A run already going when another is picked finishes with the harness it started with, and a conversation is only carried on by the harness it began with; the next request with another harness starts a new one.
Each harness is run its own way, streaming what it does as a line of JSON per event, which is read into the same reply, tool calls, usage, and result, whichever harness wrote it:

- Claude Code is `claude -p`, in auto mode, the system prompt given with `--append-system-prompt`, a conversation carried on with `--resume`, and a copy of one with `--fork-session`.
- Codex is `codex exec`, with `--full-auto` and `--json`, the prompt read from its standard input, a conversation carried on with `resume`.
- OpenCode is `opencode run`, with `--format json`, a conversation carried on with `--session`.

Codex and OpenCode take no system prompt of their own, so it is given ahead of the prompt, marked off from it. Neither can carry on a copy of a conversation, so a question asked while another is running starts a new conversation with them instead. The notes, commit messages, and prompt titles are written with a small model where the harness can be told one, Claude Code's haiku, and with the harness's default model otherwise.
When the harness picked isn't installed, a run on the host fails saying that it can't be run, as any run that can't be started does. A run in a container uses the harness in its image instead, and fails, where Podman isn't installed or can't run, as the [ContainerEnvironmentScope](../container-environment/index.md#container-environment-scope) says.

#### Protected Locations

Only a run on the host has protected locations. A run in a container has none, since nothing it mustn't touch is mounted there, as the [ContainerEnvironmentScope](../container-environment/index.md#container-environment-scope) says: it isn't guarded, and its harness is given no rule against reading or editing anything.
Where the harness takes rules for what its tools may do, as Claude Code does with `--disallowedTools`, a run on the host is told what its mode keeps it off. A Code task is told it may not edit the spec location, and a Spec task the code location; the application puts back whatever changes there all the same, and says so in the task's output as a passive notice, never an error, as the [TaskTableScope](../../ui/components/task-table/index.md#task-table-scope) says. A Code task and a question from the Ask tab are also told they may not read the spec location, alongside that, so they read the compiled reference instead, as the [ModeSystemPromptsScope](../prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts-scope) says. This rule is only a nudge, and doesn't enforce anything, since a shell command can still read the files, and nothing puts anything back or stops the run when one does. A harness that takes no such rules is told nothing of either.

#### Feeding

A task's run is given its prompt as a stream of messages: Claude Code with `--input-format stream-json`, each message written as a line of JSON on the harness's standard input, which stays open for as long as the run lasts. The run's first message is the task's compiled prompt, as ever, and each message sent to the task after it, from the [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope), is written as another.
A message reaches the harness when it finishes what it is doing rather than interrupting it, so a run that is mid-tool-call takes it once that call is over. The harness echoes each message back as it takes it in, with `--replay-user-messages`. A message taken in between turns is answered with a result of its own, and one taken while a turn is under way is answered within that turn, sharing its result.
A run can also start work in the background that goes on after its turn ends: Claude Code's subagents, shell commands run in the background, such as a long build, and any other kind of background task it adds later. Every such task holds the run open, whatever its kind. The run keeps each background task that has started and not yet ended, by its id: one starts when the harness says a task has started, and ends when the harness notifies that task's end, whatever it ended as. A notification doesn't say what kind of task it is, so it is matched by id against those seen starting. The harness wakes the run when a background task ends, so it can act on what came of it.
A result no longer ends the task on its own. The run's last result is the first to come once every message sent has been taken in and no background task is still going. A result that comes before then, while a message sent hasn't been taken in or a background task is still going, is only an answer: the task keeps running, its input stays open, and more can still be sent to it. At the last result the run's input is closed, but the task is only shown as finished once the harness's process has exited as well, and it then finishes in the state of that last result; until the process exits, the task keeps running. A process that exits without a last result finishes the task as a run with no result does, failed. A run that is stopped closes its input and ends straight away, whatever is still going in the background, since its whole process group is ended with it.
Codex's `codex exec` and OpenCode's `opencode run` read a single prompt and can't be fed more while they work, so a task running with either takes its prompt as ever and can't be sent more.
Questions, the palette's file search, the one-off runs, and the notes, commit messages, and prompt titles each take a single prompt, as ever.

#### Images

Images attached to a prompt, as the [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) says, are given to the harness as it takes them: to Claude Code as image content blocks, base64-encoded with their media type, in the same stream-json user message as the prompt's text, after it; to Codex with an `--image` argument per image; and to OpenCode with a `--file` argument per image. A message fed to a running Claude Code task carries its images the same way, and a Claude Code run that isn't fed more but has images is given its prompt as a stream-json message too, so the images can go with it. Codex's options end with `--` before the prompt when it is given images. Questions take images as tasks do.

#### Context

The harness keeps its context between requests instead of starting fresh each time. Each lane of the [PromptSendingScope](../prompt-mode/sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) carries on a conversation of its own, so nothing a task of one lane read reaches a task of the other: the spec lane's, carried on by Spec tasks and a Chain prompt's spec steps, and the code lane's, carried on by Code tasks, a Chain prompt's code step, and Freeform tasks. Each task sent carries on its own lane's, and since a lane runs one task at a time, two tasks never carry on the same conversation at once. A Chain prompt's steps hand on to each other as text, the prompt and what the step before replied, as the [ModeSystemPromptsScope](../prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts-scope) says, so the handoff crosses lanes whatever each lane's conversation holds. When the project is opened, each lane carries on the latest conversation among its own tasks in the history, a Chain task by the lane of the step it was.
A run in a container keeps its lane's sessions in that lane's volume, and a run on the host where the harness keeps them on the host, as the [ContainerEnvironmentScope](../container-environment/index.md#container-environment-scope) says, so a conversation is only carried on where it began: turning the project's "Run code tasks in a container" option on or off starts the code lane on a new conversation at its next task.
Questions from the Ask tab share a separate conversation of their own, and when the project is opened they carry on the latest conversation among the questions saved with it. A question asked while another is running carries on a copy of that conversation, so questions running at the same time never write over each other. A conversation is only carried on in the project it began in, each open project keeping its own tasks' and questions' conversations while it is in the background, and if one can't be carried on, the next request starts a new one. Each run applies its own prompt's systemPrompt, even when it carries on a conversation begun in a different mode. The palette's file search always starts fresh.
A conversation can be left for a new one, from the chat input's New conversation button, as the [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) says, which leaves the conversation of the lane it is used for: the next request in it starts a new conversation with no context, and the one left is not carried on again, not by a run of it still going, nor by the project's history. Leaving it is kept with the project, as the [ProjectDataScope](../project-data/index.md#project-data-scope) says, so a project opened after a lane's or the questions' conversation was left starts a new one there too, rather than carrying on the latest conversation in its history, until a run after the reset begins one of its own. How much context a conversation holds is known from what the harness reports with each reply: everything the model was given, cached or not, and what it wrote, as of its latest reply; replies of subagents don't count.

use /lib
from ../project-data import ProjectDataScope
from ../project-directory import ProjectDirectoryScope
from ../prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts import ModeSystemPromptsScope
from ../prompt-mode/sending import PromptSendingScope
from ../settings-window import SettingsWindowScope

export scope HarnessIntegrationScope:
    concept: {HarnessIntegrationConcept}

concept HarnessIntegrationConcept:
    pitch:
        Uses the one-off version of a coding harness for the selected
        ${ProjectDirectoryScope}: `claude -p`, `codex exec`, or `opencode run`,
        whichever the user chose. Each run carries on a conversation, so the
        harness keeps its context between requests.

    shape: {HarnessIntegrationShape}

shape HarnessIntegrationShape:
    description:
        Should always run in auto mode.

        The project's system prompt, its system template filled in, as the
        @{ModeSystemPromptsScope} says, is appended to the harness's own
        system prompt, for example with `--append-system-prompt`, the same for
        every prompt of a conversation whatever its mode. The compiled
        systemPrompt of a prompt's hidden anchor, its mode's instructions,
        heads the prompt's own message instead.

        The prompt is given to the harness on its standard input, and what the
        harness does is streamed back as it happens. A task's run takes its
        prompt as a stream of messages rather than a single one, so it can be
        fed more while it works, as its feeding says.

        Its directory, which a system prompt's HARNESS_DIRECTORY stands for,
        is that of the harness in use: .claude, .codex, or .opencode.

        Spec tasks, a Chain prompt's spec steps, and questions run the harness
        in a container the application owns, as the
        @{ContainerEnvironmentScope} says, which holds only what their mode
        may use; Code tasks and a Chain prompt's code step do too while the
        project's "Run code tasks in a container" option is on. Every other
        run, Code while the option is off, Freeform, and the application's
        own, runs the harness on the host, in the project directory. Either
        way the harness is run, prompted, and read just as this says.

    harnesses:
        The harness in use is the one picked in the @{SettingsWindowScope}:
        Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode, Claude Code until another is picked.
        It is remembered for the user, as the @{UserPreferencesScope} says, not
        for a project. Every run the application starts goes to it, the tasks,
        the questions, the palette's file search, the one-off runs, and the
        notes, commit messages, and prompt titles it writes, and everything
        else works the same whichever it is. A run already going when another is picked
        finishes with the harness it started with, and a conversation is only
        carried on by the harness it began with; the next request with another
        harness starts a new one.

        Each harness is run its own way, streaming what it does as a line of
        JSON per event, which is read into the same reply, tool calls, usage,
        and result, whichever harness wrote it:

        - Claude Code is `claude -p`, in auto mode, the system prompt given
            with `--append-system-prompt`, a conversation carried on with
            `--resume`, and a copy of one with `--fork-session`.
        - Codex is `codex exec`, with `--full-auto` and `--json`, the prompt
            read from its standard input, a conversation carried on with
            `resume`.
        - OpenCode is `opencode run`, with `--format json`, a conversation
            carried on with `--session`.

        Codex and OpenCode take no system prompt of their own, so it is given
        ahead of the prompt, marked off from it. Neither can carry on a copy of
        a conversation, so a question asked while another is running starts a
        new conversation with them instead. The notes, commit messages, and
        prompt titles are written with a small model where the harness can be
        told one, Claude Code's haiku, and with the harness's default model otherwise.

        When the harness picked isn't installed, a run on the host fails
        saying that it can't be run, as any run that can't be started does. A
        run in a container uses the harness in its image instead, and fails,
        where Podman isn't installed or can't run, as the
        @{ContainerEnvironmentScope} says.

    protectedLocations:
        Only a run on the host has protected locations. A run in a container
        has none, since nothing it mustn't touch is mounted there, as the
        @{ContainerEnvironmentScope} says: it isn't guarded, and its harness is
        given no rule against reading or editing anything.

        Where the harness takes rules for what its tools may do, as Claude
        Code does with `--disallowedTools`, a run on the host is told what its
        mode keeps it off. A Code task is told it may not edit the spec location, and a
        Spec task the code location; the application puts back whatever
        changes there all the same, and says so in the task's output as a
        passive notice, never an error, as the @{TaskTableScope} says. A Code task and a question from the Ask
        tab are also told they may not read the spec location, alongside that,
        so they read the compiled reference instead, as the
        @{ModeSystemPromptsScope} says. This rule is only a nudge, and
        doesn't enforce anything, since a shell command can still read the
        files, and nothing puts anything back or stops the run when one does. A harness that
        takes no such rules is told nothing of either.

    feeding:
        A task's run is given its prompt as a stream of messages: Claude Code
        with `--input-format stream-json`, each message written as a line of
        JSON on the harness's standard input, which stays open for as long as
        the run lasts. The run's first message is the task's compiled prompt,
        as ever, and each message sent to the task after it, from the
        @{ChatInputScope}, is written as another.

        A message reaches the harness when it finishes what it is doing rather
        than interrupting it, so a run that is mid-tool-call takes it once that
        call is over. The harness echoes each message back as it takes it in,
        with `--replay-user-messages`. A message taken in between turns is
        answered with a result of its own, and one taken while a turn is under
        way is answered within that turn, sharing its result.

        turn ends: Claude Code's subagents, shell commands run in the
        background, such as a long build, and any other kind of background

        matched by id against those seen starting. The harness wakes the run
        when a background task ends, so it can act on what came of it.

        among its own tasks in the history, a Chain task by the lane of the
        step it was.

        A run in a container keeps its lane's sessions in that lane's volume,
        and a run on the host where the harness keeps them on the host, as the
        @{ContainerEnvironmentScope} says, so a conversation is only carried on
        where it began: turning the project's "Run code tasks in a container"
        option on or off starts the code lane on a new conversation at its

        Questions from the Ask tab share a separate
        conversation of their own, and when the project is opened they carry on

        asked while another is running carries on a copy of that conversation,
        so questions running at the same time never write over each other. A

        The project's system prompt, its system template filled in, as the
        @{ModeSystemPromptsScope} says, is appended to the harness's own
        system prompt, for example with `--append-system-prompt`, the same for
        every prompt of a conversation whatever its mode. The compiled
        systemPrompt of a prompt's hidden anchor, its mode's instructions,
        heads the prompt's own message instead.

        harness does is streamed back as it happens. A task's run takes its
        prompt as a stream of messages rather than a single one, so it can be
        fed more while it works, as its feeding says.

        Its directory, which a system prompt's HARNESS_DIRECTORY stands for,
        is that of the harness in use: .claude, .codex, or .opencode.

        in a container the application owns, as the
        @{ContainerEnvironmentScope} says, which holds only what their mode
        may use; Code tasks and a Chain prompt's code step do too while the
        project's "Run code tasks in a container" option is on. Every other
        run, Code while the option is off, Freeform, and the application's
        own, runs the harness on the host, in the project directory. Either
        way the harness is run, prompted, and read just as this says.

    harnesses:
        The harness in use is the one picked in the @{SettingsWindowScope}:
        Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode, Claude Code until another is picked.

        for a project. Every run the application starts goes to it, the tasks,
        the questions, the palette's file search, the one-off runs, and the
        notes, commit messages, and prompt titles it writes, and everything
        else works the same whichever it is. A run already going when another is picked

        carried on by the harness it began with; the next request with another

        than interrupting it, so a run that is mid-tool-call takes it once that
        call is over. The harness echoes each message back as it takes it in,
        with `--replay-user-messages`. A message taken in between turns is
        answered with a result of its own, and one taken while a turn is under
        way is answered within that turn, sharing its result.

        turn ends: Claude Code's subagents, shell commands run in the
        background, such as a long build, and any other kind of background
        task it adds later. Every such task holds the run open, whatever its
        kind. The run keeps each background task that has started and not yet
        ended, by its id: one starts when the harness says a task has started,
        and ends when the harness notifies that task's end, whatever it ended

        matched by id against those seen starting. The harness wakes the run
        when a background task ends, so it can act on what came of it.

        A result no longer ends the task on its own. The run's last result is

        input and ends straight away, whatever is still going in the
        background, since its whole process group is ended with it.

        handoff crosses lanes whatever each lane's conversation holds. When

        @{ContainerEnvironmentScope} says, so a conversation is only carried on
        where it began: turning the project's "Run code tasks in a container"

        asked while another is running carries on a copy of that conversation,

I've changed the spec, but again I couldn't run `piton build` here. It fails with the same `GLIBC_2.39 not found` error, because this container has glibc 2.36. So the reference under `.claude/reference` doesn't show these edits yet, and nothing has checked them. Please run `piton build` on the host before the code step.

**Likely cause (a guess: I can't see the code or a failing run).** Questions now always run in a container. When a project opens, they carry on the latest question conversation saved with it, and that session was most likely recorded when questions still ran on the host. The questions' container volume doesn't have that session, so `claude -p --resume <id>` (or `--fork-session`) fails at once. A failed run never records a new session, so every later ask retries the same dead session ID and fails again. The app then shows only a generic "the harness reported an error", which hides Claude Code's real message ("No conversation found…").

The coding agent should first confirm this from the actual error output before relying on it.

**What I changed in `spec/scope/harness-integration/index.pi`**
- **`HarnessIntegrationShape.context`**, rewritten where it said "if one can't be carried on, the next request starts a new one":
  - Questions only carry on a conversation started in the questions' volume. They never resume one saved from host-run questions, or one whose session the volume no longer has.
  - A request whose conversation can't be carried on is never failed for that reason, and never retried on the same conversation. This covers the harness saying there's no such session (Claude Code's "No conversation found") and a conversation started elsewhere.
  - Instead, the same prompt is sent again at once as a new conversation with no context. The dead conversation is never tried again by any later request, including through the project's history.
  - A question re-sent this way is recorded and shown as starting a new conversation, with the "New conversation" divider in `AskConversationScope`.
- **New `HarnessIntegrationShape.failures`**:
  - A failed run always says what went wrong in the harness's own words: its result error or streamed error events, otherwise its stderr and exit status, quoted as written.
  - A task shows this in its output; a question shows it at the end of its answer.
  - "The harness reported an error" may only appear as a heading above what the harness said, never on its own.
  - A run that couldn't be started says why, and one Podman couldn't run defers to `ContainerEnvironmentScope.podmanAccess` from the last step.
- I added an import of `AskConversationScope` to that file.
- I wrote the understanding file at `.suspense/history/1791040980-HarnessErrorOnEveryAsk.understanding.md`.

- `HarnessIntegrationShape.context`: questions resume only sessions from their own volume, and a failed resume is re-sent once as a new conversation, after which that session is never used again.
- `HarnessIntegrationShape.failures`: show the harness's actual error.
- `AskConversationScope` (the New Conversation and Answers sections): mark the re-sent question as a new conversation, and end a failed answer with the error.
- `ContainerEnvironmentScope.podmanAccess` (from the previous step): name Podman, not the harness, when Podman can't run the container.
